pageSpec.geometryRule: Use normalized geometry as the durable target. Figma trim-pixel values are reconstruction approximations. Visual-master comparison and relational constraints outrank exact pixels.

visualAuthority.firstImpression: A bright Japanese travel-magazine profile spread compressed into one A5 page: oversized hot-pink display title, a matched pair of large resort/wedding portraits, asymmetric speech-bubble name labels, two color-coded profile sheets, and two paper-note Q&A modules. It reads as lively editorial print, not a generic wedding profile card layout.
visualAuthority.signatureMove: The page is split into a strong blue-vs-pink two-person system without becoming a rigid grid: two nearly equal portrait anchors dominate the middle, while irregular bubbles, paper vessels, tropical ornaments and Q&A modules create tactile magazine depth.
visualAuthority.composition: Top 21% is title/ornament territory; middle 30% is dominated by two large portrait prints; the next 19% is paired profile information; the bottom 24% is two large Q&A paper vessels. The page is vertically stacked but locally irregular, with deliberate overlap at portrait/name/profile boundaries.
visualAuthority.density: high but edited; the page is busy around title/photo edges and quieter inside profile/Q&A reading fields

colorBehavior.pairingRule: Blue consistently codes Shogo/Q1; pink consistently codes Shiori/Q2, but the page must still feel like one publication system rather than two isolated UI columns.
